metadataReview.note: Reviewed calendar expression: the Russian Presidential Library explicitly gives the Battle of Mukden as 6 (19) February–25 February (10 March) 1905. The source Wikidata start/end claims declare the Julian calendar; the dates shown here express that same interval as 19 February–10 March in the Gregorian calendar. JACAR independently dates Oyama’s declaration ending the battle to 10 March. This correction does not approve the CDB90 row beginning 21 February or change any force quantities.

note:
Rounded JACAR estimates for the whole battle’s opposing Manchurian forces. Loss definitions differ: Japanese killed and wounded; Russian killed, wounded and prisoners. Civilian losses are unquantified. An independent State Historical Museum account gives different estimates: Japan over 270,000 troops and 71,000 losses; Russia about 300,000 troops and 89,000 losses. These alternatives are disclosed, not combined into invented error bounds. These numerical sources do not establish equipment.

The Japanese side receives a representative Type 30 rifle infantry component in the winter field dress described by contemporary observers: drab wool overcoat, fur collar, cloth cap and canvas leg wraps. This is a reviewed seasonal illustration for Mukden, not an automatic 1904–1905 uniform, an exact regiment, or an assertion that all 250,000 men were infantry or dressed alike. Other outerwear, cap covers, ranks and unit mixtures are not reconstructed. No quantity or identity is replaced. The Russian side receives a representative Mosin Model 1891 infantry component in winter dress: a long grey-brown greatcoat, black sheepskin papakha, felt boots and folded bashlyk, based on contemporary observers and dated campaign photographs. The illustration is explicitly reviewed for winter Mukden; it is not an automatic uniform for all Russian battles of 1904–1905, an exact regiment, or a claim that all 310,000 men shared this equipment. Other headwear, cloth covers, ranks and troop types are not reconstructed. Both camps retain their existing identities and all numerical evidence.
